title: ITC-MoE: Importance-guided Token-aware Compression for MoE Diffusion Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.01296v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) offer flexible parallel decoding and increased model capacity, but their large number of expert parameters incurs substantial computation and storage costs. Existing low-rank MoE compression methods largely rely on static factorization and fixed rank allocation, which overlook the distinctive properties of MoE DLMs. Specifically, we identify two properties: cross-mode non-uniform redundancy, where parameter redundancy and sensitivity to rank truncation vary across the input, output, and expert modes, and token-wise utilization variation, where hot and cold tokens exhibit distinct spectral characteristics and expert activation patterns. To address these challenges, we propose ITC-MoE, an Importance-guided Token-aware Compression framework for MoE DLMs. ITC-MoE consists of two complementary components. translated_title: ITC-MoE：面向MoE扩散语言模型的重要性引导的Token感知压缩
translated_abstract: 混合专家扩散语言模型提供了灵活的并行解码能力和更大的模型容量，但其庞大的专家参数数量带来了巨大的计算和存储成本。现有的低秩MoE压缩方法主要依赖静态分解和固定的秩分配，忽略了MoE扩散语言模型的独特性质。具体而言，我们识别出两个特性：一是跨模式非均匀冗余，即参数冗余度和对秩截断的敏感性在输入、输出和专家模式之间各不相同；二是token级别的利用率差异，即热token和冷token表现出不同的频谱特性和专家激活模式。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了ITC-MoE，一个面向MoE扩散语言模型的重要性引导的Token感知压缩框架。ITC-MoE由两个互补的组件构成。首先，重要性引导的自适应Tucker压缩（IATC）引入了激活……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ITC-MoE框架，通过重要性引导的自适应Tucker压缩和token感知机制，针对MoE扩散语言模型中跨模式非均匀冗余与token级利用率差异两大特性进行高效压缩，显著降低计算与存储成本。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ITC-MoE, an importance-guided token-aware compression framework that exploits cross-mode non-uniform redundancy and token-wise utilization variation to efficiently compress MoE diffusion language models, substantially reducing computation and storage costs.
